title: Usefulness of Bedside Point-of-care Ultrasounds in Intensive Care Unit for Septic Patients: A Consensus Statement of the Italian Society of Echocardiography and Cardiovascular Imaging
one_line_summary: This SIECVI consensus statement provides a practical guide for implementing structured bedside point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) to evaluate hemodynamics, infectious foci, organ dysfunction, and procedural guidance in septic ICU patients.
key_pearls: **Fluid Responsiveness Assessment**: Passive leg raise or fluid challenge accompanied by **LVOT-VTI variation >12%-15%** or **IVC distensibility >18%** on mechanical ventilation reliably predicts fluid responsiveness rather than static pressure targets.

**Septic Cardiomyopathy Recognition**: Biventricular impairment occurs in **40%-60%** of septic patients and is characterized by global systolic/diastolic depression, reduced **MAPSE (<10 mm)**, impaired strain (**GLS less negative than -18%**), and reversibility within **7-10 days**.

**Lung Ultrasound Patterns**: POCUS differentiates acute respiratory failure by distinguishing **patchy B-lines with subpleural consolidations** (ARDS/pneumonia) from **diffuse symmetric B-lines with a smooth pleural line** (cardiogenic fluid overload).

**Early AKI Detection**: An elevated intrarenal Doppler **Renal Resistive Index (RRI >0.75)** in interlobar/arcuate arteries indicates increased vascular resistance and predicts early **sepsis-associated AKI** prior to serum creatinine changes.

**Abdominal Source Identification**: Bedside POCUS identifies acute calculous or acalculous cholecystitis (**gallbladder wall >3-4 mm**, pericholecystic fluid, sonographic *Murphy's sign*) and facilitates bedside **ultrasound-guided percutaneous cholecystostomy**.

**Vascular Access & DVT Screening**: Real-time ultrasound guidance is standard of care for **central venous catheter (CVC)** placement, while 2-point or 3-point compression ultrasound detects **incompressible venous segments** to rule out deep vein thrombosis.
consensus_method: Consensus statement promoted and reviewed by members of the 2024–2026 SIECVI Scientific Documents Committee.

recommendation_blocks.topic: Bedside Hemodynamic Assessment and Fluid Responsiveness
recommendation_blocks.narrative:
- Dynamic assessments (passive leg raising, fluid challenges combined with stroke volume measurements) superiorly predict fluid responsiveness compared to static pressure metrics.
- **IVC Collapsibility Index >50%** in spontaneously breathing patients suggests low right atrial pressure (**RAP**) and likely hypovolemia.
- **IVC Distensibility Index >18%** in mechanically ventilated patients indicates volume repletion and fluid responsiveness.
- **LVOT-VTI variation >12%-15%** during dynamic maneuvers serves as a physiologically sound marker of fluid responsiveness.
- Baseline **LVOT-VTI <18 cm** reflects low stroke volume, whereas **LVOT-VTI >22 cm** indicates a hyperdynamic state typical of early vasoplegic shock.

recommendations.statement: Use dynamic measures of fluid responsiveness, such as **LVOT-VTI variation (>12%-15%)** or **IVC distensibility (>18%)**, rather than static pressure parameters to guide fluid resuscitation in septic shock.

recommendation_blocks.topic: Focused Cardiac POCUS and Septic Cardiomyopathy
recommendation_blocks.narrative:
- Septic cardiomyopathy (**SCM**) is present in **40%-60%** of septic patients, presenting with global biventricular systolic/diastolic depression and left ventricular dilation that reverses within **7-10 days**.
- Quantitative systolic parameters for SCM include visual **EF <50%**, **MAPSE <10 mm**, and **GLS less negative than -18%**.
- Right ventricular (**RV**) dysfunction occurs in **50%-55%** of septic shock patients; key indices include **TAPSE <16 mm**, **RV S' <10 cm/s**, and **FAC <35%**.
- Diastolic evaluation incorporates **tissue Doppler e' <8 cm/s** and **E/e' ratio >13**.
- Transthoracic echocardiography (**TTE**) allows rapid bedside screening for infective endocarditis (*vegetations*, valvular regurgitation, or paravalvular abscesses).

recommendations.statement: Perform structured cardiac POCUS integrating **LVEF**, **MAPSE**, **GLS**, **TAPSE**, and **TDI** parameters to characterize shock phenotypes, detect septic cardiomyopathy, and screen for infective endocarditis.

recommendation_blocks.narrative:
- LUS evaluates lung aeration across 6 thoracic regions per side using standardized protocols (**BLUE protocol**).
- **A-lines** reflect normal aerated lung tissue; **B-lines** are vertical hyperechoic artifacts denoting interstitial fluid.
- Diffuse, symmetric **B-lines** with a smooth pleural line indicate cardiogenic pulmonary edema or volume overload.
- Focal or patchy **B-lines**, pleural line irregularities, subpleural consolidations, and dynamic air bronchograms support pneumonia or ARDS.
- Pleural effusions and pneumothorax (absence of lung sliding with a *lung point*) are rapidly diagnosed at the bedside.

recommendations.statement: Utilize systematic multi-zone lung ultrasound to differentiate causes of acute respiratory failure, identify infectious foci (pneumonia), and monitor extravascular lung water during fluid resuscitation.

recommendation_blocks.topic: Abdominal POCUS: Biliary Tract and Renal Evaluation
recommendation_blocks.narrative:
- Abdominal POCUS screens for infectious sources when patient transport for CT is unsafe.
- Acute cholecystitis criteria include **gallbladder wall thickening >3-4 mm**, distension (**transverse diameter >4 cm**), pericholecystic fluid, and positive sonographic *Murphy's sign*.
- Ultrasound-guided percutaneous cholecystostomy offers rapid bedside source control for high-risk nonoperative septic patients.
- Sepsis accounts for **40%-50%** of ICU acute kidney injury (**AKI**) cases.
- Intrarenal Doppler measuring **Renal Resistive Index (RRI >0.75)** in interlobar/arcuate arteries indicates elevated renal microvascular resistance and predicts AKI development.

recommendations.statement: Perform abdominal POCUS to diagnose intra-abdominal infectious sources (e.g., acute cholecystitis) and measure Doppler **RRI (>0.75)** to assess intrarenal perfusion and early risk of acute kidney injury.

recommendation_blocks.topic: Vascular Access Guidance and Deep Vein Thrombosis Screening
recommendation_blocks.narrative:
- Ultrasound guidance for **central venous catheter (CVC)** placement is standard of care, increasing first-pass success and reducing mechanical complications.
- Post-procedural POCUS checks confirm catheter wire position and rule out pneumothorax.
- **Critical** illness and central lines increase deep vein thrombosis (**DVT**) risk.
- Bedside 2-point or 3-point compression ultrasound evaluates common femoral, superficial femoral, and popliteal veins; non-compressibility of the vein is the primary diagnostic criterion for **DVT**.

recommendations.statement: Employ real-time ultrasound guidance for all central venous catheterizations and routinely perform compression venous ultrasound for DVT screening in **critically** ill septic patients.

bedside_protocol.title: Hemodynamic & Preload Evaluation
bedside_protocol.action: Assess IVC diameter and respiratory variation using a curvilinear or phased-array probe in the subcostal view. Measure baseline LVOT-VTI in the apical 5-chamber view and re-assess VTI change (>12%-15%) following a passive leg raise or fluid challenge.

bedside_protocol.title: Focused Cardiac Assessment
bedside_protocol.action: Obtain standard PLAX, PSAX, A4C, and subcostal views. Evaluate LV and RV contractility (visual LVEF, MAPSE <10 mm, TAPSE <16 mm, GLS), rule out pericardial effusion/tamponade, and inspect cardiac valves for endocarditis vegetations.

bedside_protocol.title: Systematic Lung Scan
bedside_protocol.action: Perform a 6-zone thoracic ultrasound per side (upper/lower anterior, lateral PLAPS, posterior). Assess for lung sliding, distinguish horizontal A-lines from vertical B-lines, and look for consolidations with dynamic air bronchograms or pleural effusions.

bedside_protocol.title: Abdominal Source & Renal Assessment
bedside_protocol.action: Examine the gallbladder for wall thickening (>3-4 mm), pericholecystic fluid, and stone/sludge presence. Scan the kidneys for hydronephrosis and measure intrarenal arterial Doppler Renal Resistive Index (RRI >0.75 indicates impaired perfusion).

bedside_protocol.title: Vascular Guidance & DVT Compression Ultrasound
bedside_protocol.action: Use real-time linear ultrasound guidance for central venous catheter insertion. Perform 2-point or 3-point compression ultrasound of the common femoral, superficial femoral, and popliteal veins to identify non-compressible segments.

strengths_limitations:
- **Strengths**: Comprehensive multi-organ POCUS framework specifically structured for bedside ICU management; provides standardized diagnostic cutoff values and actionable visual step-by-step interpretation tables.
- **Limitations**: Based primarily on expert consensus rather than graded evidence synthesis (GRADE framework); protocol effectiveness remains dependent on operator skill and lacks outcome-driven randomized controlled trial validation.
